title: Nonmetricity as an Affine Response in Longitudinal Elasticity
content: In this work, longitudinal elastic deformation is investigated within a 1+1 dimensional metric-affine geometric framework. The aim is to describe deformation and the associated restoring response as components of the geometric structure, rather than formulating classical spring dynamics on a prescribed geometry. Strain is defined through the difference between the reference and deformed metrics, while nonmetricity is interpreted as the response of the affine geometry to longitudinal deformation. Within this framework, a minimal quadratic action containing a canonical coupling between the deformation field and longitudinal nonmetricity is constructed. In the small-deformation limit, the field equations generate a dynamical strain-nonmetricity relation, and elimination of the nonmetricity variables reproduces the classical Lagrangian of longitudinal elasticity. Consequently, the Hooke constitutive relation, the spring constant, and the restoring force emerge from the effective limit of the geometric action. The model can further be extended to nonlinear elasticity through higher-order nonmetricity terms, while classical spring motion can be represented within the geodesic limit of an appropriate effective metric.
